subject: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia.chen@novamed.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rpatel@novamed.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist

Hi Sylvia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum while you finish internal alignment: 

What we heard from your side:
- Primary driver: reduce inference latency for clinical triage while cutting per-token cost vs current self-hosted cluster.
- Hard constraints: PHI remains on-prem for at-rest retention; models may call external APIs for non-PHI enrichment.
- Preference ranking: (1) Dedicated capacity in our cloud (data ingress controlled), (2) Private VPC deployment if procurement requires customer-managed tenancy, (3) Hosted API only for non-PHI routes.

Open technical questions we flagged for your infra team:
1) Do you have a maintained on-prem KMS / HSM for key custody if we recommend Private deployment?
2) Current GPU cluster: 8xA100, CUDA 11.6, inference runtime is Triton-based. Any existing KV cache layer?
3) Expected steady qps (inference requests) for the triage path during peak hours?

Proposed next steps (I want to keep these concrete):
- You: Share the short migration checklist we discussed (I attached an editable version) and confirm data residency requirement in writing.
- Us: Schedule a 45-minute infra-to-infra session (Jordan + Priyom + Marissa) with NovaMed infra to align on network/firewall, KMS, and model packaging.
- Commercial: We’ll draft a short dedicated-capacity scoping estimate (monthly commit + burst) after the infra sync.

Attachments: NovaMed-Migration-Checklist.xlsx (editable), SOC2-Request-Packet.pdf (overview), redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf (sample pricing).

If that looks right, can we aim to run the infra session next week? I’m available Tues/Wed morning PT.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia.chen@novamed.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the infra meeting: 

- PHI requirement: All patient-identifiable payloads must remain in our AWS account and be encrypted with a key we control. Nightly aggregated telemetry without identifiers can be sent to Redwood for quality monitoring.
- On-prem cluster: yes, 8xA100 (we run a custom Triton stack). No formal KV cache today — everything is single-request.
- Peak qps: currently ~18 qps for triage during peak. We expect that to grow to ~60 qps in 6–9 months if adoption hits target.

Please add Priyom and your infra folks to the invite; Tuesday 10:00 AM PT works for us.

One ask from procurement: can you confirm whether a private VPC option would allow us to hold the encryption key in our KMS? If not, procurement will push for a Private (customer-managed) deployment. Also we’ll need your SOC 2 documentation and an initial draft SOW for a 2-week POC.

—Sylvia
Sylvia Chen
Head of Product 
NovaMed Analytics
sylvia.chen@novamed.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia.chen@novamed.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rpatel@novamed.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist

Great — thanks for the details, Sylvia. Quick answers and confirmation: 

- Key custody: For our Private VPC / on-prem option we can integrate with customer KMS via a mutual TLS-backed gateway so the DEK never leaves your account; for Dedicated capacity we offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration with supported KMS providers. I’ll have our security engineer walk through exact flow in the infra call.
- SOC2: attached is the SOC2-Request-Packet.pdf (summary); we’ll share the full report via secure link after an NDA.
- POC: we can scope a 2-week POC focused on the triage path. Commercially we typically run a short committed window for Dedicated POCs; if you require Private/on-prem we’ll provide a separate engagement SOW.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 2027-03-30 10:00 AM PT with a proposed agenda: network & firewall, KMS integration, model packaging (ONNX vs GGUF), and POC acceptance criteria. Priyom — can you bring the dedicated pricing sketch and a POC checklist? Marissa — can you run an initial risk/rollout note for Hannah?

—Jordan

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist

Heads up team — I reviewed NovaMed’s notes and sketched an initial commercial posture: 

- 2-week Dedicated-capacity POC (recommended path given they want performance predictability): suggest 4xA100 reserved for the POC with burst to 8x for load tests. Estimated committed cost: $18k/month (POC prorated).
- Private VPC option: higher setup and runbook overhead; include an integration fee for KMS gateway and network validation (estimate one-week infra effort).
- Migration lift: we’ll support model export from Triton to ONNX/ggml packaging; allocate 2 dev days of engineering support during POC.

I’ve attached the rough pricing PDF (redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf) and updated the Migration checklist spreadsheet with the GPU details. We should present both options in the infra call and surface costs clearly.

Action items: Jordan to confirm invite; Marissa to prepare a short risk note and a proposed POC acceptance test matrix; Hannah to confirm who signs off on the SOW (sales vs legal).

—Priyom
From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia.chen@novamed.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting handoff & migration constraints — post-demo checklist

Jordan / Priyom —

Thanks everyone. Invite landed for 10:00 AM PT. Confirming: NovaMed would like to run the 2-week POC starting the week of April 12, pending SOW and NDA. Procurement wants: standard SOW draft, SOC2 link, and a short note on who will hold keys for each deployment mode (your reply above helps). We’ll also bring a small infra engineer (Ravi) who will join the call.

Please mark the POC intent in HubSpot (DEAL-1483) and I’ll circulate a short internal note after our infra sync.

—Sylvia
